hook.text: Every time you recall a memory, it becomes temporarily unstable. You must reconsolidate it to keep it.

buildup.text: Karim Nader's 2000 study shocked neuroscience: retrieved memories return to a fragile state briefly.

discovery.text: During reconsolidation, the memory can be updated, strengthened, or distorted before re-stabilizing.

twist.text: This means every recall is also an edit. Your memories change slightly each time you access them.

climax.text: Therapists use this: recalling a trauma in a safe context can rewrite the emotional tone of the memory.

punchline.text: Recall rewrites. Every remembering is a small edit.

quiz.question: What happens to a memory during reconsolidation?
options: It becomes temporarily unstable and can be updated
It is copied to a backup region of the brain
